title: CAT 2021 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Logarithms
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.explain:
We can rewrite the equation using logarithmic properties:
$\log_{10}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = -\log_{10}\sqrt{1-x^2} = -\frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1-x^2) = -\frac{1}{2}[\log_{10}(1-x) + \log_{10}(1+x)]$.
Also, $\log_{10}\sqrt{1+x} = \frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1+x)$ and $\log_{10}\sqrt{1-x} = \frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1-x)$.
Substitute into the original equation:
$5 - \frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1+x) + 2\log_{10}(1-x) = -\frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1-x) - \frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1+x)$.
The $-\frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1+x)$ cancels out from both sides.
We are left with: $5 + 2\log_{10}(1-x) = -\frac{1}{2}\log_{10}(1-x)$.
$5 = -2.5\log_{10}(1-x)$.
$\log_{10}(1-x) = \frac{5}{-2.5} = -2$.
$1-x = 10^{-2} = 0.01$.
$x = 0.99$.
Therefore, $100x = 99$.
